I am 55 years old. I have farmed this 4.1 mu for 30 years. I never went to school, not even one day. Everything I know, I learned from my own hands and from watching the neighbors who do well. My husband and I work this land alone. We have no hired help. Last year my wheat gave about 450 kg per mu and my maize about 500 kg per mu. This year I will do the same as last year, because change is dangerous and I cannot afford a bad harvest.

For the winter wheat: After the maize comes off in autumn, I rotary till the ground and plant the improved wheat seed I buy from the dealer in town. Before planting, I spread one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. The dealer says it has three numbers on the bag, but I just tell him "give me the wheat fertilizer." In the spring, when the wheat turns green and starts growing fast, I topdress with half a 100-jin bag of urea per mu. I irrigate three times: once after planting to help the seed settle, once in spring when the wheat is jumping up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for weeds after the wheat comes up, and once for bugs when the weather gets warm. I expect 450 kg per mu.

For the summer maize: After we cut the wheat in June, I rotary till fast and plant hybrid corn seed. I put half a 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows at planting time. When the corn is about knee-high, I side-dress with half a 100-jin bag of urea per mu. I irrigate twice if the sky does not give us enough rain — once when the stalks are shooting up, and once when the ears are filling. I spray twice, for weeds and then for corn borers. I expect 500 kg per mu.

I do not buy phosphorus or potassium by themselves. The compound fertilizer has some mixed in, and that is enough for me. Every jin of fertilizer costs real money that I could use for food or medicine. But I would rather put a little too much than risk the crop failing, because if the harvest is bad, we have nothing to sell and nothing to eat.
